chapters.title: Water, breakfast, a hilltop
chapters.blurb: Start with the waterfront. Share breakfast. Enjoy the Cloisters from outside—no waiting for doors.

chapters.title: The high streets
chapters.blurb: A run of good public sidewalks and historic exteriors. No museum admissions or campus shortcuts.

chapters.title: A lunch worth stopping for
chapters.blurb: Saiguette is the food anchor. The markets are optional browsing, not another required meal.

chapters.title: Plazas & a little bustle
chapters.blurb: Big-city façades and seasonal stalls. Keep the sweet stops small.

chapters.title: Above the street, beside the river
chapters.blurb: Take the High Line south, then the pedestrian esplanade to Christopher Street.

chapters.title: Stay with the central streets
chapters.blurb: This replaces the High Line and west-side loop; it is not an extra branch to collect.

chapters.title: The smaller streets
chapters.blurb: Grove and Commerce, then Washington Square and Greene Street on the recommended branch.

chapters.title: Keep the river company
chapters.blurb: This coast swap leaves out Washington Square and SoHo. Choose it for the water, not to add mileage.

chapters.title: Down Broadway to the Battery
chapters.blurb: A last look up, then open inland park paths. The finish does not need a sunset.

stops.name: Inwood–207 St A · meet here
stops.summary: 8:30 AM meet · 8:45 AM walking.
stops.detail: Find the street elevator at Broadway and W 207th Street. This is the start—not a train-platform meeting.
stops.query: Inwood-207 St A station Broadway and West 207th Street New York

stops.name: Muscota & Inwood waterfront
stops.summary: Start with water, marsh grasses, and open west paths.
stops.detail: Walk north via Indian Road / W 218, then use the open Muscota west viewing paths and Inwood waterfront near the Nature Center.
stops.query: Muscota Marsh, Indian Road, New York NY
stops.access: The East Dock is closed. Stay on signed public paths; no shoreline or railway shortcuts.

stops.name: G’s · a savory breakfast
stops.summary: Breakfast burrito if available; plain egg-and-cheese as the simple swap.
stops.detail: 634 W 207th Street. The exact-shop review recommends the breakfast burrito special: eggs, home fries, chorizo, cheddar, avocado and salsa. Ask whether it is available today. Two burritos halved can suit four grazers, not four full breakfasts; hungry walkers should order enough. The burrito price was not verified.
stops.query: G’s Coffee Shop, 634 W 207th St, New York, NY
stops.access: Check allergies, ingredients and spice before sharing; no item is certified allergen-free. Send one or two buyers and keep the doorway clear. Prices are menu snapshots before tax, not checkout quotes.
stops.hours: Sunday 8 AM–7 PM · published, not live

source.label: G's Coffee Shop | New York, NY 10034 | Menu | Order Online

sources.label: G’s Coffee Shop - Review - Inwood - New York - The Infatuation
G's Coffee Shop | New York, NY 10034 | Menu | Order Online

stops.name: The Met Cloisters · outside
stops.summary: Stone, trees, and the Fort Tryon setting.
stops.detail: Approach from Broadway/Bennett via park stairs and the public path outside Sir William’s Dog Run. Stop on the public park side of Margaret Corbin Drive to enjoy the stone exterior, then Linden Terrace and Heather Garden. Follow signs if a connector is fenced; the southern entrance adds walking.
stops.query: The Met Cloisters, 99 Margaret Corbin Drive, New York NY
stops.access: Exterior only: no museum ticket, interior, cloister courts, ticketed gardens or 10 AM opening wait. The Broadway/Arden approach is unresolved; follow signed open paths and fences. A closed approach may require the southern Margaret Corbin Circle entrance and extra walking. The line is a model, not access certification.

story.text: This is not one medieval monastery transported intact: the modern museum incorporates architectural fragments from several French cloisters.

sources.label: Medieval Art and The Cloisters - The Metropolitan Museum of Art

stops.name: Linden Terrace
stops.summary: A pause for Hudson and Palisades views.
stops.detail: Stay with the public terrace paths; this is a good place to pause before continuing south through Fort Tryon.
stops.query: Linden Terrace, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: There are hills and uneven surfaces. Respect paving works, fences, and posted diversions.

stops.name: Heather Garden
stops.summary: Follow the garden paths toward Margaret Corbin Circle.
stops.detail: Keep the garden stroll unhurried, then leave Fort Tryon toward Bennett Park. Nearby Bonnefont has a listed Jazz WaHi brunch, 11 AM–1 PM, but outdoor seating and drop-in-without-dining access are unconfirmed. The planned walk passes earlier: do not wait for it. Treat music as a bonus only if your timing naturally fits.
stops.query: Heather Garden, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Use open paved paths; planting areas are not shortcuts.

stops.name: Bennett Park
stops.summary: A small park with Manhattan’s high-point marker.
stops.detail: A brief history stop, not a skyline observation deck. Continue along the Pinehurst public sidewalk.
stops.query: Bennett Park, Manhattan, New York

story.text: That modest boulder marks Manhattan’s highest natural point—the plaque says 265.05 feet above sea level.

sources.label: Bennett Park Monuments - Highest Natural Point in Manhattan : NYC Parks

stops.name: Pinehurst & Hudson View Gardens
stops.summary: A residential streetscape, seen from the sidewalk.
stops.detail: Enjoy the building exteriors as you pass. The landscaped residential grounds are not part of the public walking route.
stops.query: Pinehurst Avenue and West 183rd Street, New York NY
stops.access: Public sidewalks only; respect residents and entrances.

stops.name: Sylvan Terrace
stops.summary: A quiet block of historic wooden houses.
stops.detail: Take in the street and house exteriors, then continue south toward Hamilton Heights.
stops.query: Sylvan Terrace New York
stops.access: Respect homes. The nearby Morris-Jumel Mansion is closed for roof work; no interior visit is included.

story.text: This little street follows the Morris-Jumel estate’s former carriage drive, lined with 20 wooden houses built in 1882.

sources.label: Sylvan Terrace in Manhattan - Atlas Obscura

stops.name: Convent Avenue at W 148th
stops.summary: Brownstone rhythm on the way through Hamilton Heights.
stops.detail: Follow public sidewalks toward Hamilton Terrace and the Grange.
stops.query: Convent Avenue and West 148th Street New York

stops.name: Kingston · an optional patty
stops.summary: Choose a patty as the one optional extra—not another meal by default.
stops.detail: 344 W 145th Street. Beef, chicken, vegan and vegetable patties are $3 posted; coco bread is $1.50. Buy a few for interested tasters. Fillings and spice are baked in, so check before ordering. Narrow takeaway shop with steep entrance stairs; send a buyer rather than the whole group.
stops.query: Kingston Bakery Harlem, 344 W 145th St, New York, NY
stops.access: Check allergies, ingredients and spice before sharing; no item is certified allergen-free. Send one or two buyers and keep the doorway clear. Prices are menu snapshots before tax, not checkout quotes.
stops.hours: Sunday 10 AM–7 PM · published, not live

sources.label: Kingston Bakery Harlem - Review - Harlem - New York - The Infatuation

stops.name: Hamilton Terrace
stops.summary: A short, handsome residential street.
stops.detail: Walk Hamilton Terrace south and continue to the Hamilton Grange exterior.
stops.query: Hamilton Terrace New York
stops.access: Stay on public sidewalks; keep stoops and entrances clear.

stops.name: Hamilton Grange · exterior
stops.summary: A look at the house, not a museum stop.
stops.detail: Use the exterior view and continue via the PUBLIC W 141st Street / Amsterdam Avenue intersection.
stops.query: Hamilton Grange National Memorial, 414 West 141st Street, New York NY
stops.access: Do not route through CCNY campus or wait for a tour. Indoor group arrangements are separate.

story.text: In 2008 they lifted Hamilton’s whole house 38 feet to clear a neighboring church porch, then rolled it into the park.

sources.label: A Monumental Move (U.S. National Park Service)

stops.name: W 141st & Amsterdam
stops.summary: The public-street connection south.
stops.detail: Use this intersection and public sidewalks toward Morningside Drive. Do not take a campus shortcut.
stops.query: West 141st Street and Amsterdam Avenue New York

stops.name: Morningside Drive
stops.summary: Stay on the upper edge, then head for St. John.
stops.detail: Follow Morningside Drive from around W 120th toward W 113th, then approach St. John from Amsterdam Avenue.
stops.query: Morningside Drive and West 120th Street New York

stops.name: Columbia Greenmarket
stops.summary: Optional westward jog for farm stands.
stops.detail: Broadway between W 114th and W 116th Streets. This is an alternative browse—not a mandatory extra loop.
stops.query: Columbia Greenmarket, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Published schedule, not live stall availability. Let a market taste replace a pastry stop.

stops.name: St. John the Divine · exterior
stops.summary: The cathedral façade from Amsterdam Avenue.
stops.detail: Look from the public sidewalk. This walk does not include the cathedral interior or depend on a garden gate being open.
stops.query: Cathedral Church of St John the Divine, 1047 Amsterdam Avenue, New York NY
stops.access: Exterior only; no admission or opening-time wait.

story.text: Construction started in 1892, and the cathedral is still unfinished—its current priorities include community programs and maintaining what already stands.

sources.label: Plan Your Visit  - Cathedral of Saint John the Divine

stops.name: The Hungarian Pastry Shop
stops.summary: A shared box of cheese puffs and strudel, if this is your extra stop.
stops.detail: 1030 Amsterdam Avenue, across from St. John. Cheese puffs/pogácsa are $2.06 posted; poppyseed or cherry strudel is $5.67. Four puffs and one strudel make a tasting box for a few people, not a meal for the whole group. If Kingston already happened, let this be a look.
stops.query: The Hungarian Pastry Shop, 1030 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, NY
stops.access: Check allergies, ingredients and spice before sharing; no item is certified allergen-free. Send one or two buyers and keep the doorway clear. Prices are menu snapshots before tax, not checkout quotes.
stops.hours: Sunday 8:30 AM–8:30 PM · published, not live

sources.label: Three Tasty Treats at The Hungarian Pastry Shop | National Trust for Historic Preservation

stops.name: Saiguette · bánh mì break
stops.summary: The lunch anchor: roast-pork shoulder bánh mì, $12 posted.
stops.detail: 935 Columbus Avenue. Two sandwiches halved can suit four light eaters; bigger appetites should get full sandwiches. Lemongrass pork is also $12 posted. The usual sandwich contains pickled jalapeño and chili mayo; check ingredients and ask about modifications if needed. Four taro-coconut mochi ($6.95 posted) can replace a later bakery sweet. No waiting for noon and no backtracking.
stops.query: Saiguette, 935 Columbus Avenue, New York, NY
stops.access: Check allergies, ingredients and spice before sharing; no item is certified allergen-free. Send one or two buyers and keep the doorway clear. Prices are menu snapshots before tax, not checkout quotes.
stops.hours: Sunday noon–8:30 PM · published, not live

sources.label: Saiguette - Review - Upper West Side - New York - The Infatuation

stops.name: 79th Street Greenmarket
stops.summary: Seasonal stands along Columbus.
stops.detail: Columbus Avenue, W 77th–W 81st Streets. Current producer leads include Union Square Pretzel Co., Francesca’s Bakery, and orchard cider/baked goods—not guaranteed attendance or inventory. Choose one ready-to-eat find only if appealing. A market sweet replaces Hungarian or Bibble; no vendor price or samples promised.
stops.query: 79th Street Greenmarket, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Optional browse; stall stock and pack-up times vary. A taste here replaces a pastry break.

stops.name: Grand Bazaar · One of a Kind
stops.summary: A little browsing at W 77th & Columbus.
stops.detail: 100 W 77th Street. The dated November 8 One of a Kind Bazaar has handmade art, design and home goods. Choose a visible meeting point and short return time before browsing. Buying is optional; no specific food vendor is promised.
stops.query: Grand Bazaar · One of a Kind, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Indoor/outdoor event; the walk does not depend on going inside.

stops.name: The Ansonia
stops.summary: A richly detailed Broadway façade.
stops.detail: Admire the exterior from the public Broadway sidewalk, then continue toward Lincoln Center.
stops.query: The Ansonia, 2109 Broadway, New York NY
stops.access: No building entry is included.

story.text: This grand building once had a rooftop farm with chickens, ducks and goats, until the health department shut it down.

sources.label: Basement Bathhouse, Rooftop Farm, Symphonies and ...

stops.name: Lincoln Center plazas
stops.summary: A change of scale: open plaza and performing-arts façades.
stops.detail: Take the outdoor public-plaza route where open. Event and security barriers determine access.
stops.query: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts New York
stops.access: No hall entry, performance, tour, or running fountain promised.

stops.name: Bibble & Sip
stops.summary: The sweet anchor: share a taro/ube cream puff, $5 posted.
stops.detail: 253 W 51st Street, Hell’s Kitchen. Black sesame cream puffs are $7 posted. If displayed, the “Soup Dumpling” cake ($14.50) is vanilla mousse with coconut-pandan jelly, not a savory dumpling; share it instead of the puffs. Walk-in flavors and stock are unverified. Mini dozens require advance ordering online; do not count on a walk-up dozen. A market sweet can replace this stop.
stops.query: Bibble & Sip, 253 W 51st St, New York NY
stops.access: Check allergies, ingredients and spice before sharing; no item is certified allergen-free. Send one or two buyers and keep the doorway clear. Prices are menu snapshots before tax, not checkout quotes.
stops.hours: Weekend 9 AM–8 PM · published, not live

sources.label: Bibble & Sip - Review - Hell's Kitchen - New York - The Infatuation

stops.name: Bryant Park · Winter Village
stops.summary: Stroll through the shops, or simply pause in the park.
stops.detail: A walk-through of the seasonal market. No skating reservation or shopping obligation; keep moving if the paths are crowded.
stops.query: Bryant Park · Winter Village, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Published shop hours; individual vendors and access can vary.

stops.name: Chelsea Flea
stops.summary: Optional antiques and vintage on the way west.
stops.detail: 29 W 25th Street. Browse only if convenient before closing, then head west to the High Line at W 23rd.
stops.query: Chelsea Flea, Manhattan, New York
stops.access: Skip this detour if arrival is near or after 5 PM. This is not Chelsea Market.

stops.name: The High Line · W 23rd to Gansevoort
stops.summary: An elevated stretch south through Chelsea.
stops.detail: Enter at the signed W23 stairs. Stay elevated south through Tenth Avenue Square toward Tiffany Overlook, then descend the signed Gansevoort stairs. Google’s leg 10 may direct an early descent; use these park instructions instead.
stops.query: The High Line, New York NY
stops.access: Use W 23rd → Gansevoort. The overnight operator dashboard showed these elevators in service but is valid only during park hours: recheck on approach. W 16th elevator and W 34th ramp are under renovation. If access or wind is unsuitable, use open street sidewalks. The closed Western Rail Yards Interim Walkway is north of this segment.

story.text: Freight trains once pulled straight into neighboring buildings to unload; the old rails preserved in the planting beds are clues to that working past.

sources.label: Turkeys on the High Line | The High Line

stops.name: Hudson pedestrian esplanade
stops.summary: Turn toward the river, then walk down to Christopher.
stops.detail: Use the mainland pedestrian esplanade from Gansevoort toward Christopher Street. No pier-tip or beach visit is required.
stops.query: Gansevoort Peninsula, 427 Gansevoort Street, New York NY
stops.access: Use the open pedestrian esplanade, not the bikeway. Pier 51 is closed despite appearing in a restroom directory; use Gansevoort or Pier 45 toilets. Pier 40 Finger Pier/Picnic House is also closed. No whole-esplanade closure is inferred.

stops.name: Christopher Street waterfront
stops.summary: A river pause before the Village streets.
stops.detail: Use the landward pedestrian esplanade at Christopher Street / Pier 45. Follow your chosen branch: West & Village turns inland toward Grove; Coast arrives after Commerce and continues south. Use signalized crossings, never the bike lane or traffic roadway. Pier 51 is closed.
stops.query: Christopher Street Pier, New York NY
stops.access: Stay on open mainland paths; a pier excursion is not required.

stops.name: Grove & Bedford
stops.summary: One of the Village’s best street corners.
stops.detail: Follow the public streets toward the bend of Commerce Street.
stops.query: Grove Street and Bedford Street, New York NY
stops.access: Grove Court is private. Sidewalk and gate views only.

stops.name: Commerce Street
stops.summary: A curved street, brick façades, a quieter pace.
stops.detail: Take in the public sidewalk view near Cherry Lane. Continue to Washington Square, or follow the selected coast alternative.
stops.query: Cherry Lane Theatre, 38 Commerce Street, New York NY
stops.access: Respect homes; no theater or private-garden entry.

stops.name: Washington Square Park
stops.summary: A loose regroup around the arch.
stops.detail: Use public park paths. A good place to decide whether to keep walking, sit awhile, or leave the route.
stops.query: Washington Square Arch, New York NY

story.text: The marble arch replaced a temporary plaster-and-wood arch erected in 1889 for the centennial of Washington’s inauguration.

sources.label: Washington Square Park Highlights : NYC Parks

stops.name: Greene Street · SoHo
stops.summary: Cast-iron façades, from Houston toward Canal.
stops.detail: Head south along Greene Street, taking the architecture in as you go. This is a street walk, not a shopping itinerary.
stops.query: Greene Street and West Houston Street New York

story.text: Those elaborate facades often imitate carved stone in cast iron, while the upper floors once held offices, storage and manufacturing.

sources.label: SoHo-Cast Iron Historic District and Extension | HDC

stops.name: Greene & Canal
stops.summary: Leave SoHo and work toward City Hall.
stops.detail: Use public sidewalks and signed crossings toward the Woolworth Building view from Broadway.
stops.query: Greene Street and Canal Street New York

stops.name: Madison Square Park
stops.summary: The central-streets alternative after Bryant Park.
stops.detail: Stay inland through Madison Square, Flatiron, and Union Square instead of taking the High Line and Village waterfront.
stops.query: Madison Square Park New York

stops.name: Flatiron Building
stops.summary: The Broadway / 23rd Street plaza view.
stops.detail: Pause at the public plaza for the exterior view. Street works and crossings govern the route.
stops.query: Flatiron Building New York

stops.name: 901 Broadway
stops.summary: Look up at the Broadway façade.
stops.detail: An exterior view from the public sidewalk while continuing toward Union Square.
stops.query: 901 Broadway New York

stops.name: Union Square Autumn Fair
stops.summary: Optional browse on E 17th Street.
stops.detail: A November 8 street fair is listed by a secondary city-events calendar. Treat it as a possible bonus, not a reason to wait or reroute.
stops.query: East 17th Street Union Square New York
stops.access: Occurrence and exact setup are not independently confirmed.

stops.name: Washington Mews · gate view
stops.summary: A small lane, seen from the public gate.
stops.detail: Approach from University Place, then continue by public sidewalks to Washington Square.
stops.query: Washington Mews University Place New York
stops.access: Do not rely on a private-gate shortcut.

stops.name: Hudson esplanade · Clarkson
stops.summary: The coast alternative continues by the water.
stops.detail: After Grove and Commerce, return to the pedestrian esplanade. This route omits Washington Square and SoHo.
stops.query: Hudson River Park Clarkson Street New York
stops.access: Stay off the bike lane and use signed crossings.

stops.name: Waterfront to Chambers Street
stops.summary: Turn inland for the Woolworth view.
stops.detail: Continue on open pedestrian paths to Chambers, then use the public street crossing and sidewalks toward City Hall.
stops.query: Chambers Street and West Street New York

stops.name: The Woolworth Building
stops.summary: Look up from the City Hall Park side of Broadway.
stops.detail: The tower is an exterior stop. Continue south on Broadway toward Bowling Green.
stops.query: Woolworth Building, 233 Broadway, New York NY
stops.access: No lobby or interior access included.

story.text: A five-and-dime magnate commissioned this Gothic cathedral of commerce, the world’s tallest building from 1913 until 1930.

sources.label: The Woolworth Building | New York Landmarks Conservancy

stops.name: Broadway & Bowling Green
stops.summary: The final downtown stretch.
stops.detail: Follow public sidewalks and signed crossings toward the Battery.
stops.query: Bowling Green, New York NY

stops.name: The Battery · inland finish
stops.summary: Finish near SeaGlass on open inland paths.
stops.detail: The goal is a comfortable finish, not the exact tip of the island. Take whichever signed inland paths are open near SeaGlass.
stops.query: SeaGlass Carousel, Water Street, New York NY
stops.access: Wharf, Gardens of Remembrance, and parts of Oval Lawn are closed. No seawall access or carousel ride promised. No sunset deadline. If the signed inland approach is blocked, finish at the open park perimeter.

directions.note: Manual park section: ascend at W23, then stay on the elevated path south through Tenth Avenue Square toward Tiffany Overlook. Descend only at the signed Gansevoort exit. Google may suggest an early street descent; do not follow that shortcut.

directions.label: K1 · High Line Gansevoort → Grove/Bedford → Commerce → Christopher waterfront
directions.note: From the Gansevoort street exit, go directly to Grove/Bedford and Commerce. Then use public sidewalks and the signalized Christopher Street crossing to the landward pedestrian promenade. Ignore any NY-9A roadway wording: never enter the traffic carriageway. No pier-tip excursion required.

directions.label: K2 · Christopher waterfront → Hudson promenade south → Chambers crossing → Woolworth
directions.note: Follow the Hudson pedestrian esplanade past Clarkson and North Moore to Chambers, not the bicycle lane. Cross West Street at the ground-level signed signals, then use Chambers / Greenwich / Park Place sidewalks to Woolworth. Google’s trail/bridge/toll labels do not certify the pedestrian lane; no toll, bridge elevator or ferry required.

directions.label: K3 · Woolworth → Bowling Green → inland Battery
directions.note: Broadway sidewalks → Bowling Green → signed open inland Battery pedestrian paths near SeaGlass. Do not enter a bicycle-only lane despite Google’s Battery Bikeway wording. Wharf closed; use the open perimeter if paths are fenced.

directions.label: O1 · Optional Columbia market connector
directions.note: Optional replacement connector before St John: adds about 0.37 mi plus browsing. Published Sunday market hours 8 AM–4 PM.

directions.label: O2 · Optional Chelsea Flea connector
directions.note: Optional replacement for leg 09: adds about 0.18 mi plus browsing. Skip near or after the 5 PM closing.

west.blurb: Take the High Line south to Gansevoort, then head directly into Grove and Commerce before returning to the river.

village.blurb: Small public streets and private courtyards viewed only from outside. Then return to the waterfront at Christopher.

variants.distanceLabel: About 18.8 mi / 30.2 km; optional detours extra.

decisions.title: How are the legs?
decisions.body: After the northern hills, take a real pause. If anyone is done, leave by subway rather than pushing through the whole island. Check current service before entering.

decisions.title: Pick one way south.
decisions.body: West & Village is the recommendation. Central streets trades the west-side loop for Flatiron and Union Square. The coast swap skips Washington Square and SoHo. These are alternatives, not add-ons.

decisions.title: Let closing time make the choice.
decisions.body: Skip Chelsea Flea near or after 5 PM. Protect the three food anchors, choose at most one extra taste, and let market sweets replace pastry breaks. Reassess legs, weather and daylight; no sunset deadline.

decisions.title: Keep the afternoon flexible.
decisions.body: Skip Chelsea Flea near or after 5 PM. Protect the three food anchors, choose at most one extra taste, and let market sweets replace pastry breaks. Reassess legs, weather and daylight; no sunset deadline.

essentials.title: Start here
paragraphs: Sunday, November 8, 2026. Meet outside the Inwood–207 St A street elevator at Broadway / W 207 at 8:30 AM; walk at 8:45. Keep the landing clear. This is not the 207 St 1 station.

essentials.title: A full day, with permission to shorten it
paragraphs: West & Village is the recommendation: about 19.3 miles. With an 8:45 AM departure, 2.5–2.8 mph moving pace, 150 minutes of pauses and 15 minutes of reserve, the model finishes around 6:25–7:15 PM. At 2.2 mph it can run past 8 PM. Hills, queues and detours can add time.

Central streets keeps the northern parks and UWS markets but skips the High Line / west-side loop: about 17.3 miles, roughly 5:40–6:25 PM with the same assumptions. Choose at Bryant, not after zigzagging between both.

Coast is about 18.8 miles: High Line → Grove / Commerce → longer Hudson promenade → Chambers → Battery, skipping Washington Square / SoHo. Same departure and pause assumptions: about 6:10–7 PM; around 8 PM at 2.2 mph. More wind exposure, not a dramatic shortcut.

Allocate 20 minutes for breakfast, 25 for lunch, 10 for Bibble and 10 for one optional taste. The remaining pause budget covers scenery, markets, toilets and regrouping. Market sweets can replace Bibble; no extra queues are free time.

Useful checkpoints: lunch around 1 PM, UWS markets roughly 2 PM, Bryant mid-afternoon. These are broad planning windows, not rendezvous appointments. Share your actual progress with anyone joining. Sunset is 4:44 PM, not a deadline.
bullets: Protect the Cloisters exterior, a proper lunch and the UWS market pair.
If the group is tiring, shorten at Bryant or finish in the Village / SoHo. That is a good day, not a failed route.
No rush to finish the island; necessary food, water and bathrooms outrank the mileage.

essentials.title: Three buys. One optional extra.
bullets: G’s breakfast → Saiguette lunch → Bibble sweet. These are choices, not mandatory purchases.
Choose one extra: Kingston, Hungarian, or a market taste—not all three. Market sweets replace Hungarian or Bibble.
Hungry people should order enough for a meal. Shared quantities are tasting examples, not a whole-group ration.
Check allergies before ordering. One or two buyers, entrances clear, sauces separate if wanted.

essentials.title: The queue rule
paragraphs: A chosen limit, not a wait prediction: skip or swap if ordering plus fulfillment is quoted over 10 minutes. Meal eating/rest time is separate from that wait limit. Simplify once or choose a swap before paying; do not abandon already-paid food. No opening-time waits, backtracking or default full-group drink round.

essentials.title: Two swaps, not two extra stops
bullets: Dutch Baby Bakery, 813 W 187th: later breakfast instead of G’s. Sunday storefront opens 7:30 AM; brunch daily 8 AM–4 PM. Try a buttermilk biscuit with two eggs; cheddar is available. Ask for takeaway, not a table hunt. Official evening closing times conflict, irrelevant to this breakfast option.

Roti Roll, 994 Amsterdam at W 109th: lunch instead of Saiguette. Sunday 11 AM–2 AM Monday. Consider a palak-paneer frankie; check filling and heat, and request chutney separately if wanted. Decide while still on Amsterdam—do not return north from Columbus.

essentials.title: Transit is a schedule, not a guarantee
paragraphs: The overnight MTA schedule listed an uptown A from Canal / Sixth Avenue at 7:39 AM, arriving Inwood–207 at 8:19:30 AM. Check actual arrivals and destination in MTA before travelling; this guide has no live train feed.
November 6–9 bulletin: no 1 north of Dyckman through Monday 5 AM. Uptown C/local A run express 59→125; downtown A/D run local 125→59. No Manhattan J until Sunday 10 PM.

essentials.title: Access comes before the line on a map
bullets: Muscota East Dock is closed: use the open western viewing paths.

The reference uses Broadway/Bennett park stairs, not the unresolved Broadway/Arden connector or a subway elevator. If blocked, follow signed public routes toward Margaret Corbin Circle; an unmeasured street detour may add 30–45 minutes. Never cross fencing.
Cloisters exterior only—no admission, interior, ticketed gardens or waiting for opening.
High Line: published 7 AM–10 PM. Manually stay elevated from W23 to Gansevoort; Google leg 10 may suggest an early descent. Recheck access on arrival; use streets if unsuitable.
Pier 51 and Pier 40 Finger Pier/Picnic House are closed. Use the open pedestrian esplanade, not the bike lane.
Battery Wharf, Gardens of Remembrance and parts of Oval are closed. Finish on signed open inland paths or the perimeter; no harbor-edge endpoint promised.
Street construction may require pedestrian diversions. Follow signs/flaggers, never fences or a campus shortcut.

essentials.title: Carry the basics
bullets: Wind shell
Removable warm layer
Comfortable broken-in shoes and socks
Filled water bottles; refill or purchase en route as available
Light snacks
Charged phone and power bank/cable
Blister protection
Outdoor fountains are not a dependable November water plan. Buy water or refill where permitted.
Use a toilet before setting off. No museum admission or purchase is needed for the six public facilities listed below.

essentials.title: Fun without homework
bullets: At a natural pause: best bite so far? At finish: biggest surprise? No scoring sheet or pressure to buy.
Optional neighborhood-detail photos only when already stopped; no required list or completion target.
Choose a visible meeting point and short return time; point out one amusing object, buying optional. Ask before close photos of strangers.

essentials.title: Bathroom gaps: do not wait until urgent
paragraphs: The six timed anchors leave a long gap between Fort Tryon and Lincoln Center. Use Fort Tryon proactively and plan an additional permitted stop before that becomes uncomfortable. Café/customer access is not assumed.

NYC Parks also lists public toilets at Bennett Park (W185 / Fort Washington), Sheltering Arms Playground (W129 / Amsterdam), and Sol Bloom Playground (W91–92 / Columbus). These are optional nearby backups: exact Sunday doors and closure status have not been verified. Agency-wide guidance says most park restrooms operate 8 AM–4 PM; do not treat that as each facility’s confirmed hours.

On Central streets, use Bryant before heading south. Washington Square’s public toilet is listed by NYC Parks, but its evening opening is not confirmed and the route can arrive after general park-restroom hours. Do not rely on it as the only late-day option.
